summary: Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor in philosophy at New College, Oxford (c. 1967–1996) and held a post at King's College London (c. 1996–2013).

Jonathan Lear is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University, and the Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held posts at Yale, Cambridge, and the University of Chicago, serving as John U. Nef Distinguished Service Professor (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. Educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley, he became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College, Yale University, and Yale Divinity School. He held positions at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean of the College (1977–1982).

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the International Buddhist University and completed a PhD in 1998 at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with Albrecht Wezler, David Seyfort Ruegg, and S. A. Srinivasan.

Jongcheol Lee is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo (1994) under Ekyo Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (2001).

Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies who studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He held multiple posts there, serving as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor emeritus (1970–1989), alongside leadership roles at the Historical Society of Ryukoku University and other institutions.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. After a fellowship at the Dutch Research Council, he became an associate professor at Leiden University in 1993.

Josef Horovitz was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He completed doctoral studies under Eduard Sachau around 1895–1898 and held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 1889. He held academic posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich, where he was professor (1896–1925).

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian who studied at the University of Munich. He held faculty posts at the University of Graz (c. 1892–1909), the University of Vienna (c. 1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (c. 1925–1928).
Josef van Ess was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn from around 1953 to 1959. He held a post at the University of Tübingen from approximately 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Andrew Sittler was a religious studies scholar who studied at Wittenberg University. He taught at the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (c. 1943–1957) and served as professor of theology at the University of Chicago (1957–1973).

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar educated at Canterbury School, Dartmouth College, Columbia University, and the universities of Paris and Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933) and was a faculty member at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow from around 1832 to 1839. He worked at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and served as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, from 1847 to 1885.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was an Indologist and geographer educated at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania and was a professor at the University of Minnesota (1964–2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion educated at University College School and the University of London. He served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford (c. 1876–1915) and taught at the University of Oxford (c. 1889–1915).

Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, INALCO, EPHE, and the University of Paris. He served as conservator at the Musée Guimet (1913–1941) and directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan beginning in 1934.
